# VideoFocus

> VideoFocus is an iPhone and iPad app for parents that plays only the YouTube channels and videos a parent has approved. No recommendation feed, no autoplay, no comments, with screen time limits, bedtime and a parent passcode. Independent app by Venture Ink LLC; not affiliated with or endorsed by YouTube or Google.

## Key facts
- Platforms: iPhone and iPad, iOS 17.5 or later. Not on Android or TV.
- How it works: the parent sets a passcode, creates a profile per child, searches YouTube inside the app and approves whole channels or single videos. Approving a channel includes its new uploads automatically. Children see only approved content and can search only within it.
- Screen time: a different daily limit for each weekday, bedtime lockout, a warning at 90%, extra time only with the parent passcode. Counts only minutes of actual playback.
- Playback: YouTube's official embedded player; VideoFocus never downloads or re-hosts videos. The device must be able to reach www.youtube.com.
- Ads and privacy: no ads, trackers or third-party analytics from VideoFocus. YouTube's player can show YouTube's own ads. No Shorts feed (a channel's own Shorts can appear among its videos).
- Price: free for one child profile on one device. Family Plan: US$3.99/month or US$39.99/year, two-week free trial, Family Sharing supported; adds unlimited child profiles, multiple devices, screen time schedules and bedtime.
- Children do not need a Google or YouTube account.
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/videofocus-kids-video-library/id6795647933

## Sister app
- PodFocus: Podcasts for Kids (same developer, Venture Ink LLC) applies the same parent-approved approach to podcasts: a curated kid-safe catalog with profiles from preschool to teen (older kids can have grown-up podcasts approved one at a time), per-child profiles, daily listening limits, parent PIN, offline downloads. Free, no ads in the app, no subscription. iOS 18+. https://apps.apple.com/app/podfocus-podcasts-for-kids/id6774022255 · https://podfocus.app

## How it compares
- YouTube Kids: filters a kids-only catalog; its approved-content mode works only within that catalog and turns search off. VideoFocus approves any YouTube channel. YouTube Kids is free and runs on TVs; VideoFocus does not.
- Supervised YouTube (Family Link): content levels plus channel blocking; cannot restrict a child to specific channels.
- Apple Screen Time: can limit or block YouTube as a whole, not by channel. Used together with VideoFocus to keep the YouTube app and browsers off a child's device.
